svg.title: ULTRA-SATISFACTORY as a four-channel tracker module
svg.desc: The editor screen of an Amiga-style music tracker, playing a song called ULTRA-SATISFACTORY. A grey embossed panel holds a stack of numeric fields with arrow buttons (POS, PATTERN, LENGTH 0004, ITEMS 0140, RECIPES 0211, BUILDINGS 0477, SAMPLE, PER MIN, CYCLE S, POWER MW), a button grid (PLAY, STOP, EDIT, PATTERN, OVERCLOCK, SPAGHETTI, and the three tabs OBJECTIVES, ITEMS, BUILDINGS with purple, pink and blue lamps), a logo plate reading ULTRA-SATISFACTORY, companion app for Satisfactory, every recipe, one click apart, and four small scopes with yellow traces. Below: SONGNAME ULTRA-SATISFACTORY, unofficial fan project; SAMPLENAME and MACHINE, which step through real recipes (for example Reinforced Iron Plate, Assembler, 5 per minute, 12 second cycle, 15 MW); and a status strip: tempo 125, 1 row = 1 sec, and a STATUS line that reads ALL RIGHT, then FUSE BLOWN. AGAIN (the OVERCLOCK lamp blinks), ALL RIGHT-ISH, SCREW BOX FULL, PIPE CLIPS WALL and NOBODY SAW THAT. Four black pattern windows labelled SMELTER, CONSTRUCTOR, ASSEMBLER and MANUFACTURER scroll blue note data under a fixed grey edit row. Each note is a machine finishing a craft cycle, so a 2 second recipe plays every 2 rows and one pattern is one minute of factory. A fat green-to-yellow VU bar per channel jumps on every note, and a yellow arrow pointer idles over the OVERCLOCK button.
